mentl/95b05cf:
Priority served: the 6.3 modal sweep rule-by-rule, the first loop-sized item
the standing cursor names. The rule taken was feedback-under-negation, which
6.3 records as waiting only on 3.6's build -- and 3.6 built. The iteration set
out to pin it and measured it UNSOUND instead, so what lands is the kill, the
peer and the repros, not a green leg.

THE `<~` SITE DOES NOT JOIN THE RECURRENCE BODY'S ROW. It substitutes its own,
and the substitution errs in both directions at once.

DROPPED: a forbidden effect performed inside the recurrence body does not
reach the enclosing row. `fn cycle() with !E` around
`((prev) => prev + bump()) <~ Delay(1)` checks CLEAN and reports only
T_OverDeclared "body only uses Memory + Alloc". That is an !E soundness hole
at the feedback carrier, the crown's own class. Isolated to `<~` alone by
control: the same op called directly refuses, and the same lambda passed
through `fn apply(f) = f(1.0)` and called refuses, both E_EffectMismatch --
lambda-row propagation is healthy everywhere else.

ADDED: `<~ Delay(3)` reaches Memory + Alloc, so `with !Alloc` around it
refuses. Isolated by a second control -- the identical lambda and comparison
with the `<~` removed judges Pure, so the charge is the feedback site's own.

SYNTAX is trued in the same landing: its `<~` section claimed the delay
line's slots are "declared, never allocated, so depth costs nothing per tick
and the !Alloc row survives at any N". The row half is refuted at N=3. The
declared-slots half is marked UNTESTED rather than refuted, because what was
measured is the ROW and the same site drops an effect it must carry -- the
row at that edge is untrustworthy in both directions, so it cannot be read as
evidence about the emit either way.

The two crucibles stand as repros and are deliberately NOT wired to a frontier
leg: a leg asserting either measured behaviour would canonize the bug, and a
permanently red leg would block every later landing. They are named from the
peer instead.

mentl/95a4cff:
The wheel attaches /// doc comments before nearly every top-level
decl (2181 sites across src+lib). The seed's $parse_stmt_p had no
TDocComment arm — when the dispatch saw token kind 29 it fell
through to the expression-statement default and called parse_expr,
which mis-parsed the doc-token and produced garbage AST nodes that
infer would then unify against, surfacing thousands of spurious
diagnostics.

Fix: at $parse_stmt_p entry, if the leading token is TDocComment
(29), advance past it and re-dispatch. The infer-side Documented
(tag 128) arm at walk_stmt.wat:467-471 is already wired for the
wheel-canonical Documented(doc, inner) wrapper that the named
follow-up Hβ.first-light.documented-stmt-substrate produces.
For first-light surface, dropping the doc is sufficient.

Verified on src/types.nx (heavy /// density across 23 ADTs):
TDocComment no longer surfaces as parse failure; remaining
diagnostics are H.2.a (let-stmt destructure) + missing prelude fn
references.
